title: Integer squared moduli in the seventh cyclotomic field
source_title: Schweitzer Miklós Mathematical Competition 2022: Előzetes megoldások 2022
author_responsibility: Original Hungarian statement and printed solution; see the source caveats and exact source ranges.
material_provenance: Fixed author PDF retained by the corpus. Physical PDF page references.
difficulty_reason: Sufficiency passes to the quadratic subfield via the printed Gauss sum and factors split primes there. Necessity lifts the squared modulus to an odd power of it via the cyclotomic field norm, whose prime-ideal norms force even exponents for the three forbidden residue classes.

statement_spans.label: 6. Legyen ε egy primitív hetedik egységgyök, with the printed proposer names.

proof_spans.label: Megoldás (kitűző) through the final norm-cube argument and square. Include 6.1–6.4 in order.

dedup.scope: 180295 studies arithmetic functions evaluated at random binary forms. It does not classify integer squared moduli in Q(ζ₇); no equivalent task or claim located.

readability.basis: Fixed report PDF. Printed selected solution is read directly in the stated physical page range.

source_caveats: In Lemma 6.4 the report prints Z[λ]/P even though it defines P in Z[ε]. The same paragraph explicitly uses ε+P and the quotient of Z[ε] by (ε−1), and the next paragraph defines the norm on ideals of Z[ε]. Preserve the printed symbols and identify the quotient from those source lines.
